description.narrative:
Governance institutions have been strengthened to assist in implementing inclusive development strategies. With that aim, a collaboration was established with the Turkish Confederation of Tradesmen and Craftsmen (TESK) in 2020 to establish Information Centres at local unions of tradesmen and craftsmen.
Capacity of staff and systems have been strengthened to reach out to informal businesses and their workers to provide information, public employment services, support refugees’ access to decent employment and fundamental principles and rights at work. With support from the Government of Germany, The ILO provided technical knowledge and resources, developed guidance and manual documents and capacity building for information centres to operate effectively.

description.narrative: The European Green Deal Action Plan of Turkey was approved in August 2021 (Presidential circular 2021/15). This Action Plan is relevant for the promotion of decent work and a just transition in the rural economy as it covers several key policy areas including green and circular economy, as well as sustainable agriculture and climate action. In support of the Government’s efforts to operationalize the European Green Deal Action Plan for Turkey, green job opportunities in agriculture and rural areas have been promoted for refugees (Syrian and non-Syrian) and host community members. In particular, to harness the potential of rural women for the revitalization and enhanced social cohesion in rural areas, an innovative partnership at local level enabled the creation in July 2020 of the Meryem Women’s Cooperative. The Cooperative aims to create green job opportunities in agriculture targeting around 135 rural women, both refugees and host community members. The cooperative has endured even during the COVID-19 pandemic, including by diversifying their activities into the production of producing personal protective equipment (face shield and surgical mask production). During 2020 and 2021, with support from the United States' Bureau of Population, Refugees and Migration (USBPRM), the ILO provided technical support to promote green job opportunities in agriculture and rural services, such as recycling services, at local level. The ILO provided capacity development to refugees (Syrian –non-Syrian) and host community members. Concerning rural women’s economic empowerment, in partnership with the Adana Municipality, the ILO supported the establishment of the Meryem Women’s Cooperative. The ILO also provided capacity development to this Cooperative, while the municipality allocated farmland for its agricultural activities.

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security implemented a work-based-learning (WBL) scheme to increase the employability of disadvantaged groups in the labour market, i.e. the youth, women and persons with disabilities, by supporting their vocational and professional development during the period of employment.
The WBL programme targets mainly youth and women among the Syrian refugees under temporary protection and Turkish citizens. In order to roll-out the programme addressing the needs of the labour market in the most effective way, a pilot implementation phase was initiated for 200 beneficiaries in 2020. In addition to the technical skills development pillar, the WBL programme has succeeded to create capacities in labour rights and decent work principles for participants. As a result, the programme has enabled participants to develop their hands-on skills as well as supporting formal and decent jobs. The ILO contributed to the design and implementation of the WBL programme and facilitated skills development opportunities for Syrian refugees and Turkish citizens.
In the course of pandemic, the majority of the face-to-face training activities had to be reformulated for online delivery. The ILO established a virtual learning platform (ILO Academy) to support both online and blended training delivery. The platform currently hosts two training programmes: 1) Basic Labour Market Training (BLMS) targets new entrants and job seekers among the Arabic speaking refugees and the host communities, and aims to equip them with knowledge on international labour standards, national labour legislation, public employment services and it supports adaptation to work life. 2) Zero Tolerance to Violence Training Programme aims to prevent violence and harassment at work and home.

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Labour and Social Security revised the Action Plan of National Employment Strategy (2014-2023) in 2020 in a tripartite discussion where ILO provided technical support. Main intervention areas of the revised Action Plan is the provision of skills to improve youth employment and addressing the NEET problem in Turkey. ILO provided technical support and guidance to the Ministry of Labour and Social Security in the revision and update of the Action Plan of National Employment Strategy of Turkey in 2020 through participation to the tripartite technical meetings and provision of comprehensive written inputs to the Action Plan in which youth employment and NEET is one of the critical issues addressed by the Ministry and the constituents.
ILO further supported the constituents in addressing the youth employment problem in Turkey through evidence-based knowledge generation and awareness raising. In that regard, the ILO established a cooperation with UNDP with reference to the ILO-UNDP Framework of Action to organise joint actions on youth employment in 2020. The ILO published a report on “The Youth and COVID-19: Access to Decent Jobs amid the Pandemic” addressing the current situation of the NEET in the course of the pandemic and regarding their expectations. This assessment shed a light to ILO in holding meetings with the local labour market actors. Two validation workshops with around 750 young people were organized. In order to respond to the high interest from the young people as well as the policy makers, four Instagram live broadcasts on; digitalization and access to decent work and on rural development, rural youth and access to decent work, and two on creative industries were organized, reaching around 3000 viewers in 2020 and 2021. Additionally, many other sorts of training such as Java 101 Bootcamp, Python&Angular, PhP Laravel Bootcamp, and retailing training were delivered to young Turkish citizens and refugees in Turkey to increase their skills.
Currently moto-courier training, call centre training, Turkish language courses are in the agenda under the partnership of the ILO and Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality. By the end of 2021 the total number of beneficiaries was approximately 1500.

description.narrative:
To protect labour rights and promote safe and secure working environments for all workers, including migrant workers, in particular women migrants, and those in precarious employment, the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and the ILO implemented a tailor-made workplace adaptation programme (WAP. The WAP aims to support sustainability of employment, intercultural communication and social cohesion at the workplace for refugees (Syrians and non-Syrians) and host community members working together. In 2020, the WAP introduced new modules on core labour rights, anti-discrimination, gender equality and intercultural dialogue at workplaces. The programme implementation continued online during the COVID-19 crisis. WAP supports the labour market integration of refugees as well as host community members. WAP is a tailor made programme designed by the ILO. A cadre of trainers consisting of academics is in charge of programme delivery.
The ILO developed mechanisms to ensure online implementation of the WAP. Based on the global collaboration between the ILO and H&M, the WAP implementation efforts in Turkey echoed the global partnership through WAPs implementation in H&Ms supply chains.
